When a downstream AI agent then refines what it receives, it is not refining the idea; it is refining a degraded, decontextualized shadow of it, and in doing so, it forecloses the very ambiguity that would have allowed the human's incubation process to later resolve the idea's meaning organically. The cost is not merely fidelity loss — it is the premature closure of a cognitive opening.

raw_input.content: Current voice and quick-text capture pipelines are fundamentally unreliable as inputs to downstream agent refinement because they systematically discard three categories of signal that are irreplaceable: prosodic emphasis (which word the speaker stressed, indicating salience), ambient and temporal context (where, when, and immediately after what the idea was captured), and intent class (is this a task, a question, a creative seed, or an emotional reaction?). Word-error rates on conversational, spontaneous speech still hover well above those on read speech, and even when transcription is accurate, a flat text string cannot encode that the user said "I want a *meeting* about the proposal" versus "I want a meeting about the *proposal*" — two utterances with meaningfully different downstream actions. When downstream refinement agents receive a decontextualized transcript, they are forced to hallucinate missing intent, producing confident but wrong elaborations that are harder to correct than a blank canvas.

raw_input.content: The "premature closure" framing in m_sq_003_0002 is precisely correct and can be grounded in concrete pipeline mechanics: when ASR systems flatten prosodic contours into uniform word-confidence scores, they do not merely lose emphasis — they actively misrepresent salience by treating all tokens as equally weighted. This is not a recoverable error at the refinement stage; it is an upstream information-theoretic loss. The fix must happen at capture — either through prosody-aware ASR models that output pitch and energy annotations alongside tokens, or through multimodal capture that preserves temporal metadata, recent app context, and location as side-channels that constrain intent disambiguation before the transcript is handed off.
